## What's new
- Replaced native terminal tab groups with custom tabs: immediate creation, smooth close and reorder motion, hover-close controls, equal adaptive widths that scroll into a tab-list picker when they run out of room, a Close Tab action for VoiceOver, and the Settings shortcut at the right edge. - Added live tab dragging between windows without restarting sessions, with a window preview when a tab is dragged out, deep links for focusing a tab from another app, and exact focus restoration. - Added a compact single-session header that gives unused tab-strip space back to the terminal grid, with a global “Always show tabs” setting and a per-window “Show Tab Bar” control. - Added protocol-driven tab status indicators: badges pulse while work is running, briefly confirm success, and retain background failures, while explicit progress reports use a display-synchronised lower bar. - Added Move Tab to New Window and Close Other Tabs to the Window menu, and Move Tab to New Window to each tab's context menu, so tabs can be managed without dragging. - Reduced the shipped universal app download size.
## Changed
- Removed the per-window tab and pane limit while window restoration is off; with restoration on, an oversized window now restores its selected tab and as many others as fit instead of a single fresh pane. - Reduced graphics memory retained by hidden tabs while preserving their sessions and stable rendering.
## Fixed
- Stopped the Input Dock from filling in late when a tab opens: the prompt chevron and the typing hint are now drawn from the tab's first frame instead of appearing together once the shell finished starting, and the caret no longer changes size and place when they do. - Stopped the Input Dock from inviting a command while the shell is still using the screen: a startup file that asks a question, such as an ssh key passphrase, keeps its own prompt without “type a command” appearing underneath it. - Preserved the working directory when several tabs are opened in quick succession. - Stopped false close warnings while a shell is still starting, without discarding typeahead or real jobs. - Closing tabs whose shells are still starting no longer briefly stalls the interface. - Applied UI Scale changes immediately instead of waiting for the next interaction.

## What's new
- Added lazy custom flat themes in Settings, with Ghostty and Kitty import and editable templates created from the current theme.
## Changed
## Fixed
- Fixed colour emoji rendering in additional tabs and splits. - Kept plain-text and program-authored links whole, hoverable, and clickable after terminal resizing wraps them across rows. - Hardened automatic updates and disabled Check for Updates while Sparkle cannot start another check. - Fixed Find so CJK text, combining marks, and emoji clusters match without losing exact grid highlighting. - Restored terminal windows to their previous macOS Spaces with their split layouts, pane directories, focus, and last visible terminal text while fresh shells start. - Kept typing responsive when other native tabs are hidden by suspending their display clocks. - Restored terminal rendering after macOS wakes sleeping displays or moves a window between displays. - Kept Command-hover file and folder links stable when another native tab was hidden.

## What's new
## Changed
- Renamed the instant Cursor motion option from Snap to Off.
## Fixed
- Ran configured Nushell startup commands before the first prompt, kept prompts correct and responsive while typing and resizing, and pasted file paths literally in Nushell and fish, including names with spaces, quotes, and newlines. - Kept application, terminal, and Control shortcuts working after switching to a non-Latin keyboard layout. - Moved every shell's input to the top when Input Dock is disabled, including custom launchers. - Moved the live shell cursor to clicked positions in the input line, with or without Input Dock. - Deleted selected Input Dock text with Backspace or Forward Delete. - Made Input Dock selections start from blank space and keep the caret on the active edge, including emoji, with a native text-selection pointer over selectable terminal text.
